items.title: Hidden and forgotten 2D materials are discovered with AI
items.excerpt: Linköping University researchers used AI to mine materials databases, finding 33 overlooked MXenes and making 11 new ones, plus a seconds-fast synthesis route without external heating (Science).

items.title: A new physics-informed AI tool aims to predict wildfire spread in real time and assist wildfire response
items.excerpt: NYU Tandon built a wildfire digital twin pairing a physics fire-spread model with an AI solver fed by live satellite, weather and sensor data; forecasts matched observed burn areas with up to 94.6% overlap on three past fires.

items.title: The human surfaceome: AI flags potential cell surface drug targets overlooked by major databases
items.excerpt: Five protein databases agreed on only 188 of 5,546 surface proteins; a Claude Sonnet 4.6-based agent reviewing the literature classified surface proteins at 95.7% accuracy versus ~90% for UniProt (bioRxiv preprint).

items.title: Fluent language makes a hallucinatory chatbot just as credible as a curt, flawless one
items.excerpt: Radboud University found a fluent chatbot giving false facts was rated as intelligent and pleasant as a terse accurate one, and about 80% of participants missed the errors (Computers in Human Behavior: Artificial Humans).

items.title: AI often passes for human, but asking follow-up questions can trip it up
items.excerpt: Across 72,000+ judgments, people identified AI-generated captions, word associations and replies only slightly above chance (53-57%), but got better at spotting chatbots as live questioning went on (Nature Human Behaviour, NTU Singapore).

items.title: AIs fail to reliably detect AIs in reverse Turing tests
items.excerpt: Seven LLMs acting as interrogators in 238 reverse Turing tests flagged only 3 of 98 AI respondents as AI, judging AIs human more often than real people (Paris Cité University, Computers in Human Behavior Reports).

history_match.title: Researchers dispute whether AI has passed the Turing test

items.title: 10 minutes is all it takes for AI assistance to erode your motivation, study shows
items.excerpt: In problem-solving experiments, people who used AI to get answers were more likely to give up and fail once the help was removed than people who never used AI.

history_match.title: Using AI for just 10 minutes erodes your ability to persist at hard things

items.title: OpenAI just scooped mathematicians' work on another million-dollar problem
items.excerpt: Using an internal LLM, OpenAI released a formal proof tied to the quantum chromodynamics Millennium problem, scooping an independent proof in progress by Anthropic's Levent Alpoge and Northwestern's Ethan Sussman.

history_match.title: The inside story behind OpenAI's million-dollar math proof

items.title: The sleep framework: A new way for LLMs to retain knowledge in continual learning
items.excerpt: Google Research adds a 'sleep' phase to continual learning so LLMs can integrate new facts and improve reasoning while mitigating catastrophic forgetting and fixed knowledge cutoffs.

items.title: Bringing foundational models to the front lines of TB screening
items.excerpt: Google describes five years of moving from TB-detection benchmarks to open foundation models that can be tuned and deployed at the point of care in high-burden communities.

items.title: Empowering frontline maternal care with AI-assisted ultrasound
items.excerpt: A prospective multi-center study shows AI blind-sweep ultrasound lets non-sonographers with low-cost probes deliver expert-level gestational age assessments.

items.title: Q&A: How AI came to model the 'messy' human mind
items.excerpt: MIT's Benjamin Lindquist discusses how randomness and irrationality were built into early AI models designed to mimic human creativity.

items.title: To detect deepfake videos, researchers turn to the physics of light
items.excerpt: An optical deepfake-detection technique claims 97.8% accuracy while using less energy than digital neural networks of similar performance.

history_match.title: This light-powered AI can spot deepfakes with nearly 98% accuracy

items.title: Study: AI Could Speed Quantum Threats - And Help Build Defenses
items.excerpt: A new analysis argues AI could accelerate quantum threats to encryption while also helping organizations prepare post-quantum defenses.

history_match.title: Riverlane and NVIDIA use AI to speed up quantum decoder calibration

items.title: People are taking an unapproved weight-loss drug. AI found something surprising
items.excerpt: AI analysis of nearly 150,000 Reddit posts surfaced symptom reports linked to unapproved retatrutide - increased appetite, sleep disturbance, elevated heart rate - that differ from clinical-trial results.

items.title: Yonsei University Researchers Develop Mamba State-Space Neural Decoder to Enable Real-Time Quantum Error Correction
items.excerpt: A Mamba-based QEC decoder matches Transformer decoders like AlphaQubit in accuracy while cutting complexity from O(d^4) to O(d^2), aiming at real-time decoding. (Off-list: on-list quantum outlets had no fresh AI-decoder item.)

history_match.title: SEEQC Combines Chip-Based Processing With NVIDIA AI to Improve Quantum Error Correction

items.title: Gothenburg and Chalmers Researchers Develop Modular Graph Neural Decoder for Surface Code Memory and Lattice Surgery
items.excerpt: A modular graph neural network decoder for surface-code QEC outperforms traditional decoders and adapts across hardware and lattice-surgery operations. (Off-list exception.)
